title: Tuesday · Remembrance assembly, SpacesEDU and French
arrival: Answer attendance, then hand in any forms. Get ready for our 9:00 am assembly.
note: Remembrance Day assembly starts at 9:00 am; its end time is not confirmed. After the assembly, use any time before snack/recess for Nevermoor and/or continuing Health feelings and needs. Keep the morning flexible; no morning fraction lesson. After recess, continue existing SpacesEDU work if laptops are available; otherwise prepare the same work on paper. French remains 12:35–1:35. If the class is ready, begin a short introduction to fractions after French; do not assume Monday’s deferred fraction lesson was taught. Preserve snack at 10:20, recess 10:35–10:50, lunch 11:50–12:35, cleanup around 2:00 and dismissal at 2:35. Tomorrow is Remembrance Day: school is closed. No new homework or posting deadline.

blocks.title: Welcome and attendance
blocks.firstAction: Answer attendance, then hand in forms.

blocks.title: Get ready for the assembly
blocks.firstAction: Follow directions to prepare and move to the assembly.
blocks.notes: Use the school’s transition arrangements and arrive ready for the 9:00 am start.

blocks.time: 9:00 am · end time to be confirmed
blocks.title: Remembrance Day assembly
blocks.firstAction: Listen respectfully and follow the assembly directions.
blocks.notes: Start time is confirmed by Daryl. Follow the actual assembly ending; do not assume a fixed duration. Adjust the optional follow-up rather than rushing.

blocks.time: After assembly · if time before snack/recess
blocks.title: Nevermoor and/or Health · if time
blocks.firstAction: Follow your teacher’s choice: continue Nevermoor or practise feelings and needs.
blocks.notes: Choose Nevermoor, Health or a short part of each according to the actual time available. Nevermoor: resume the actual class bookmark, listen/read, and invite one idea supported by a story detail; record the stopping point. Health: continue the existing feelings-and-needs work, not a new assignment. Use a fictional situation such as two friends wanting different games. Model a possible feeling (disappointed), a need (choice or belonging) and a request (Could we take turns choosing?). More than one feeling or need may fit. A request allows a no; respect stop signals and seek a trusted adult if unsafe. Students may speak, draw, point, write, observe or pass. Do not require personal conflict, grief or war disclosures. Stop for the usual break routine; carry unfinished learning forward.
studentSteps: If reading: start at our bookmark and explain one idea using a detail from the story.
If doing Health: use the made-up situation to suggest a feeling, a need and a respectful request.
Explain how to respect a no or stop. You may speak, draw, point, write or pass.

blocks.title: Snack
blocks.firstAction: Have your snack and tidy your space.

blocks.title: SpacesEDU · if laptops are available
blocks.firstAction: Find the existing work or posting your teacher identifies.
blocks.notes: Laptops are proposed, not booked or confirmed. If available, continue unfinished SpacesEDU postings and respond to existing feedback. Check instructions, work quality and the intended private audience before posting. Do not assume all Monday postings are complete. If devices or access are unavailable, prepare or improve the same existing work on paper; upload later at school. This is continuation time, not a new assignment or posting deadline.
studentSteps: Read the existing instructions and feedback.
Continue or improve the work and reflection for that activity.
If laptops are unavailable, prepare the same work on paper.
Ask for help where needed and save your progress.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.firstAction: Follow our outside-play and lunch routine.

blocks.title: Fractions introduction · if ready
blocks.firstAction: If we begin fractions, get paper and a pencil ready to make equal parts.
blocks.notes: Optional first introduction after French, not a follow-up to an assumed Monday lesson. Begin by checking what equal parts and one whole mean. Use identical paper strips: one strip is one whole. Fold or draw each into four equal parts, name each part one fourth, then build five fourths with two strips. Group four fourths as one whole, leaving one fourth: 5/4 = 1 1/4. If ready, students build six fourths with the same-size whole and explain 6/4 = 1 2/4. Check understanding by asking what stays the same (the whole and size of each part) and why both names show the same amount. If equal parts need more work, stay with halves and fourths rather than pushing mixed numbers. If the class is not ready to start, continue existing quiet work or reading instead and carry the introduction forward.
studentSteps: Make equal parts in identical paper strips; keep the whole the same size.
Build or draw the amount your teacher models and explain what one part means.
If ready, show six fourths and explain how many wholes and extra fourths you have.

blocks.title: Save, tidy and move
blocks.firstAction: Save your work, complete classroom jobs and join a short movement break when directed.

blocks.title: Pack up and dismissal
blocks.firstAction: Check your belongings and prepare for dismissal.

backups: The assembly ends when the school programme finishes; no precise ending or reading/Health duration is assumed.

Laptops after recess are not confirmed. Prepare existing SpacesEDU work on paper if devices or access are unavailable.
Fractions may begin after French. Monday’s fraction lesson was deferred, not recorded as taught; start from what students can actually show.
No new homework, upload or posting deadline is added.
